1. QUERY shortcut lacks coverage ✓ Resolved 🐞 Bug ⚙ Maintainability
>
>Description >
> >
>The new query() shortcut is not included in the existing method-shortcut test, so tests would pass
>if it were absent or registered with the wrong HTTP method. This leaves the newly introduced public
>API behavior unverified.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py[R303-309]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6202/files#diff-426c9d8938b9fecd1513d2b0bbf638f37abab0b3d18f00769ddb8f5fb0e8ae90R303-R309) > >```diff >+ @setupmethod >+ def query(self, rule: str, **options: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[T_route], T_route]: >+ """Shortcut for :meth:`route` with ``methods=["QUERY"]``. >+ >+ .. versionadded:: 3.2 >+ """ >+ return self._method_route("QUERY", rule, options) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The PR adds query() at src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py:303-309, while the existing parametrized
>shortcut test only enumerates get, post, put, delete, and patch at
>tests/test_basic.py:55-64. The implementation delegates through _method_route, so a test should
>verify that the resulting rule accepts the QUERY method rather than merely relying on the shared
>implementation.
>
> > [src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py[303-309]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/855f80e9208df9f86ae38fd884df0ae2787d0b2b/src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py/#L303-L309) > [tests/test_basic.py[55-64]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/855f80e9208df9f86ae38fd884df0ae2787d0b2b/tests/test_basic.py/#L55-L64) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The new `Scaffold.query()` shortcut is not covered by the existing method-shortcut test, so incorrect method registration could go undetected. > >## Issue Context >The shared test currently covers only `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete`, and `patch`. Add `query` coverage using the test client’s generic request method if it does not expose a `query()` convenience method. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- tests/test_basic.py[55-64] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
